correctness.rationale: Lucas parity makes f(s) a product over the binary submask downset D(s). For distinct s,t the symmetric difference has at least 2^{min(popcount(s),popcount(t))} elements, so independent elliptic bits give an exact product covariance and a uniform m^{-1/(8 log 2)} bound for the second moment of the spatial Cesàro mean. Chebyshev/Borel–Cantelli on m_j=ceil(j^{12}) plus bounded interpolation prove almost-sure spatial cancellation. Independent geometric holding times for the monotone negative-step count, with a weighted Kolmogorov strong law and negligible terminal block, transfer cancellation to the conditional time-averaged cross-bracket. The bounded two-dimensional martingale increments then satisfy the functional martingale CLT with identity limiting covariance. Exact checker asserts 4,376 finite algebraic instances but does not replace the proof.

originality.rationale: Hamza and Tournier (2026), arXiv:2610.01658v1, Section 4.3, Proposition 11 and Corollary 12 establish annealed, not quenched, normality for exactly the static uniformly elliptic cardinality-grouped coefficient environment and flag its quenched counterpart as unresolved. The separate functional martingale criterion of Collevecchio et al. (2022) does not give the static-environment almost-sure cross-bracket law. The present proof derives that law from a uniform biased Pascal-submask covariance bound and geometric occupation. Previously available independent-time or fully sampled Boolean coefficients do not imply it. Actual scientific semantic searches found no stronger result asserting the same quenched conclusion; possible general orthogonal-product theorems remain a residual historical-priority risk.

value.rationale: The 2026 motivating article isolates the static cardinality regime and explicitly proves only annealed convergence, leaving quenched normality unresolved. The new result settles the whole uniformly elliptic independent static-bit class, including heterogeneous biases, by connecting binary-submask decorrelation to geometric occupation. This is a natural structural probability question, not an arbitrary finite slice or a mere change of notation; the general strong-law method also explains why temporal resampling is unnecessary in this regime.
